overall: Atlanta is warming steadily through the early afternoon on a mostly sunny day with low dewpoints (53.6°F) and light winds, reaching 82.4°F by 13:30 ET. Conditions are running noticeably cooler than the NWS text forecast of 87°F would suggest, with NWP models (ECMWF 80.7°F, NBM 80.6°F) already surpassed and HRRR (83.5°F) nearly so. The active Flood Warnings are for the Satilla River in far southern Georgia and have no bearing on Atlanta's temperature today.

The NWS text forecast of 87°F appears to be a significant outlier relative to both observations and NWP consensus, and the intraday bucket model strongly disagrees with it, assigning only ~2.9% probability to 86–87°F.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max at 82.4°F, a current warming velocity of +1.8°F/hr, a predicted peak near 14.7h ET (roughly 1–1.5 hours away), and sparse cloud cover, the temperature should add roughly 2–3°F before leveling off, pointing to a daily high near 84–85°F. The INTRADAY model assigns 64.3% probability to the 84–85°F bucket and D1_NOW agrees at 57.7%, making this the high-confidence outcome. Confidence is moderately high given strong intraday signal convergence, though minor uncertainty remains around peak timing (NWP models peak later at 16–17h, which could allow a touch more warming).
